sentences.text: Shri Kunar Singh and Shri Aman Raghuwanshi, learned couns  the appellant.
Shri Vikram Pipple - learned Public Prosecutor for respon Heard on I.A.No.1445/2026, second application under Section 389 of Cr.P.C. for suspension of jail sentence and grant of bail to appellant.
His first application was dismissed as withdrawn on 26.06.2025.

This appeal assails the judgment dated 25.10.2024 passed by the Special Judge (POCSO Act)
Gwalior in Special Case No.195/2023 whereby, appellant has been convicted under Sections 366 and 376(1) of IPC and Section 3/4 POCSO Act with maximum sentence of 10 years RI with default stipulation.
Learned counsel for appellant submitted that the appellant is innocent and has falsely been implicated in the crime.
The learned trial Court has erred in convicting the appellant without appreciating the evidence in right perspective.
Appellant has already suffered more than 2 years 5 months of incarceration as pre and post trial confinement.
Learned counsel for the appellant further submitted that prosecutrix went along with the appellant on her own volition.
There is no physical or sexual assault committed by the appellant over the prosecutrix.

Learned counsel for the appellant has relied upon the statement of Dr. Rajkishori Dandotiya in which she stated in her 2 CRA-14254-2024 para-6 that no definite opinion in regard to the sexual or physical assault with the prosecutrix can be given.
Learned counsel also submits that DNA is also suspicious because the sample taken from recovered bed-sheet is matched with DNA of appellant not with prosecutrix.
Appellant has already suffered more than 2 years 5 months incarceration.
He was on bail during trial, however, he did not misuse the liberty so granted.
Amount of fine has been deposited by him.
There is no likelihood of early disposal of the appeal in near future.
The appellant shall abide by all the conditions as may be imposed by the Court.
On these premises, prayer for suspension of sentence has been made.
Learned counsel for the respondent opposed the application and prayed for its rejection.

Considering the arguments advanced by learned counsel for the parties and attending facts and Vijay Verma vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 2 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/40052375/
1 circumstances of the case, especially looking to the fact that final hearing of the appeal shall take some time, without commenting on merits of the case, I.A. is hereby allowed.

sentences.text: Subject to depositing of fine amount, if not already deposited, and on furnishing personal bond of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the concerned trial Court, the remaining jail sentence of appellants shall remain suspended and he be released on bail.
He is further directed to mark his appearance before the Office of this Court on 28.10.2026 and on subsequent dates given by the Office in this regard, till final disposal of this appeal.

The appellant shall not move in the vicinity of victim and shall not be 3 CRA-14254-2024 a source of embarrassment or harassment to the victim and her family members in any manner, otherwise benefit of grant of suspension of jail sentence shall stand cancelled automatically without any reference to the Court.

Appellant shall not try to contact the victim and her family members by himself, through somebody else or through any electronic device, otherwise, benefit of suspension of sentence shall be immediately withdrawn.
A copy of this order be sent to the concerned Court below for compliance.
Certified copy as per rules.
(PUSHPENDRA YADAV) JUDGE Ashish*
